findings.title: New table widget renders hardcoded empty data, breaking dashboards under the feature flag
findings.body: In `tableResultComponent`, when the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is on, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` instead of the existing `StyledSimpleTableChart`. Both `columns` and `tableData` are hardcoded to empty values, so the actual query results (`result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, `fieldAliases`) are discarded entirely. Any organization with this flag enabled will see empty table widgets in dashboards regardless of the data returned by the API. The wiring of real data into the new component is missing.

findings.title: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with dict values(), misaligning events when any node is missing
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, fetches them via `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` (which returns a dict that omits missing nodes and whose `.values()` ordering is not guaranteed to match the requested key order), then constructs ErrorEvents with `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. If any error event node is missing from nodestore, or the returned dict order differs, the wrong `event_id` is paired with the wrong event data, and the `if data is not None` filter can drop the wrong entries. This produces incorrect error titles/messages/timestamps sent to Seer for the replay summary. Iterate over `events` items keyed by node_id (or use `get_multi`'s mapping back to event ids) instead of `zip`.

findings.title: Full unauthenticated request bodies logged at info level
findings.body: The endpoint logs `logger.info("browser_report_received", extra={"request_body": request.data})` for every request. This is an unauthenticated, CORS-enabled public endpoint (permission_classes = ()) that accepts arbitrary JSON payloads from browsers, including report `body` contents, URLs, and user agents (potential PII). Logging the entire body at info level in production will also produce unbounded log volume for large or malicious payloads. The request body should be omitted or logged at debug with size limits.

findings.title: Editing bodies of already-shipped data migrations
findings.body: Migrations 0917 and 0920 have had their data-conversion logic replaced with a no-op and a comment claiming they "had an error and was never run". These migrations have already shipped in releases, and self-hosted installations (or any environment where they did run, e.g. the 0917 migration before the 0920 revision was cut) have them recorded as applied. Mutating applied migrations creates divergence: environments where 0917 ran and inserted GroupSearchView rows will also run 0921 ("rerevised"), which may duplicate or conflict with rows created by 0917, since 0917 can no longer be inspected for what it did. The corresponding test for 0917 was also deleted. The safe pattern is a new corrective migration, not rewriting history; at minimum this needs a clear statement that no environment (including self-hosted) executed these.

findings.title: Refactor swaps useApiQuery options for useQuery defaults, enabling retries and refetch-on-focus
findings.body: The previous implementation used `useApiQuery` with `{staleTime: 0, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: false}`. The new `useQuery` call passes only `enabled`, `queryKey`, and `queryFn`, so react-query defaults now apply: up to 3 retries with exponential backoff on failure and refetch on window focus. Since this hook drives search-bar attribute-key suggestions (called per keystroke/interaction), failed requests will now be retried 3 times and refetch when the user refocuses the window, increasing load on the trace-items attributes endpoint and changing observed latency/error behavior. Preserve the original query options (retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false) or set them explicitly.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only filtered when a search query is present
findings.body: `sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns the unfiltered sorted list when `searchQuery` is empty, and only applies the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(...)` filter inside the search branch. So `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` are still shown when the user has not typed anything, but disappear as soon as they type — inconsistent behavior. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied unconditionally, before the search-substring filter.
